query: What per-arm sample sizes are needed to detect 3% and 5% mean percent weight-change differences at 6 months with 80% and 90% power using a repeated-measures mixed model; what ICC and variance estimates are realistic?

response.query: What per-arm sample sizes are needed to detect 3% and 5% mean percent weight-change differences at 6 months with 80% and 90% power using a repeated-measures mixed model; what ICC and variance estimates are realistic?
response.answer: To detect 3% and 5% mean percent weight-change differences at 6 months with 80% and 90% power, per-arm sample sizes of 40-60 are needed. Realistic ICC and variance estimates are typically around 0.1-0.2 and 0.01-0.05, respectively.
